name: binsider
summary: Terminal UI tool for analyzing ELF binaries with static and dynamic analysis, string extraction, linked library inspection and hexdumps.
use_cases: inspect ELF sections, segments, symbols and relocations
trace system calls and signals of a running binary
find URLs and passwords embedded in a binary
features: show binary file info and linked libraries

steps.command: cd /tmp && curl -sSLO https://github.com/orhun/binsider/releases/download/v0.3.2/binsider-0.3.2-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz && tar xzf binsider-0.3.2-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz && mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && cp binsider-0.3.2/binsider ~/.local/bin/
steps.purpose: Download v0.3.2 x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu release tarball, extract, copy binsider to ~/.local/bin

setup.command:
cat > /tmp/drive.py <<'EOF'
import os, pty, sys, time, select, re, struct, fcntl, termios
# usage: drive.py "<keys>" binsider args...
keys = sys.argv[1].encode().decode('unicode_escape').encode()
args = sys.argv[2:]
pid, fd = pty.fork()
if pid == 0:
    os.environ['TERM'] = 'xterm-256color'
    os.execvp(args[0], args)
fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack('HHHH', 50, 200, 0, 0))
os.kill(pid, 28)
buf = b''
def pump(t):
    global buf
    end = time.time() + t
    while time.time() < end:
        r, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.1)
        if r:
            try: buf += os.read(fd, 65536)
            except OSError: return
pump(2)
for k in keys.split(b'|'):
    if k:
        os.write(fd, k); pump(2)
os.write(fd, b'q'); pump(1)
_, st = os.waitpid(pid, 0)
txt = re.sub(r'\x1b\[[0-9;?]*[A-Za-z]|\x1b[()][A-Z0-9]|\x1b[=>]', ' ', buf.decode('utf-8', 'replace'))
print(re.sub(r'[ \t]+', ' ', txt))
sys.exit(os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(st))
EOF

pitfalls.actually_needed: No Rust toolchain needed: prebuilt binary binsider-0.3.2-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz from GitHub releases works
It is a full-screen TUI with no non-interactive output; automated checks needed a pty driver script (/tmp/drive.py) using -t <tab> and sending keys

pitfalls.readme_said: execute the binary and trace the system calls
pitfalls.actually_needed: Under gVisor (this box) tracing fails with ESRCH: No such process; needs a regular Linux kernel with ptrace

judge.observed: binsider renders the General tab with file info and a Dependencies list for /bin/ls, the Static tab with File Headers and Notes, and --help prints 'binsider 0.3.2' with usage.

features.feature: show binary file info and linked libraries

features.note: no failed check in the log; Tracing system call error: ESRCH: No such process; box is gVisor with limited ptrace

evidence.quote: all within a user-friendly terminal user interface!
Just dive into the binaries by running `binsider`:
**Binsider** can perform static and dynamic analysis, inspect strings, examine linked libraries, and perform hexdumps, all within a user-friendly terminal user interface!
You can analyze the ELF layout (such as sections, segments, symbols, and relocations)
execute the binary and trace the system calls, signals, and the program's execution flow
discovering interesting strings such as URLs, passwords, and other sensitive information
You can retrieve general binary file information, including file size, ownership, permissions, date, and linked shared libraries
You can analyze the ELF layout (such as sections, segments, symbols, and relocations)
execute the binary and trace the system calls, signals, and the program's execution flow
`binsider` is able to extract strings from the binary file
